admission.authority: direct user continuation after the main-backed fixed residue-wheel complexity boundary and priority scheduler
admission.reason: Compose the retained BRC multiplier x vertical lattice with classical B-smooth factor-base relations and GF(2) dependency algebra while preserving the exact observer/provenance boundaries needed for congruence reconstruction.

methods.name: BRC multi-strip smooth-relation lattice / GF(2) carrier facade
capabilities: exact cross-multiplier relation extraction x^2-D=mN with shared x^2=D mod N semantics
exact B-smooth factorization carrier with full exponent and parity projections
incremental GF(2) dependency detection retaining relation provenance
exact square-congruence reconstruction and gcd witness surface
round-robin shallow relation sampling across all admissible multiplier strips
methods.core_law: Every smooth BRC lattice point x_i^2-D_i=m_i N gives x_i^2 congruent D_i mod N, so relations from different multiplier strips combine in one factor-base algebra without any condition on the product of multiplier labels. The exponent parity projection is sufficient for GF(2) dependency detection, but full exponents and x provenance must be retained to reconstruct the square congruence. Multiplier provenance may be forgotten only after relation extraction when future operations are restricted to dependency/congruence construction.
methods.hard_boundary: Dixon, QS, MPQS, SIQS, B-smooth factor-base collection, GF(2) linear algebra and congruence-of-squares factoring are classical prior art. The reference implementation uses trial division and incremental bitset elimination and is not a production sieve. Finite relation-yield/factoring-budget improvements are not asymptotic complexity results or novelty claims. The minimum-gap heap optimizes only next-gap ordering, not proved smoothness probability. No Foundation promotion is made.
